Sections follow the manuscript. Each heading names the display items it produces; every number in the
paper is written by a chunk here (to `results/`) or by the companion notebook.

| | |
|---|---|
| R | ≥ 4.2: `phyloseq`, `vegan`, `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `patchwork`, `car`, `edgeR`, `DESeq2`, `metagenomeSeq`, `TITAN2`, `ape` (`V.PhyloMaker2` optional: the tree is supplied) |
| Data | the Zenodo data deposit (unpacked folder `data/`); set `PAPER_DATA` to its path, or keep the default `submission/data` |
| Modules | the `.R` files of this folder, next to this document |
| Runtime | c. 30 min, mostly TITAN2 and the permutation tests |

Run order: this document, then `Paper_figures.ipynb`.

# Setup

```{r paths}
library(phyloseq); library(vegan); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)

## The project root. Everything else is derived from it, so this is the only
## line to change on another machine.
PROJECT    <- Sys.getenv("PAPER_PROJECT", "/Users/mathieuvanhove/Desktop/Work/DeepImpact/Weeds_wheat")
SUBMISSION <- file.path(PROJECT, "submission")

## Everything the analysis reads lives under submission/data, staged by
## stage_submission_data.sh, which mirrors the layout of paper_1/data. Point
## DATA_DIR at the original tree instead and it still works -- the layout is
## the same -- but the staged copy is what the submission ships, and it carries
## the harmonised species names.
DATA_DIR   <- Sys.getenv("PAPER_DATA", file.path(SUBMISSION, "data"))   # or the unpacked Zenodo data deposit
RES_DIR    <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "results_v4")
MATRIX_DIR <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "matrice_phase1", "df")
META_DIR   <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "df")
OUT_DIR    <- Sys.getenv("PAPER_OUT", file.path(SUBMISSION, "results"))   # where every result is written

TITAN_DIR <- file.path(RES_DIR, "TITAN_Full_Dataset")
MEQO_DIR  <- file.path(RES_DIR, "mEQO")   # optional, legacy (mEQO is not used in the paper)

## Differential abundance: BOTH roots, and this is deliberate. The same
## filenames exist under data/<method>_species/ and results_v4/<method>_species/
## and they are different runs -- for edgeR the complete file (the one that
## actually contains the wheat x wheat contrast) is in a different root for
## each soil. da_resolve() in da_codetection.R picks per file by checking which
## copy contains the control; a fixed root reproduces one soil and breaks the
## other. DA_SEARCH is the ordered list it searches.
DA_SEARCH <- c(DATA_DIR, RES_DIR)
DA_DIRS   <- file.path(rep(DA_SEARCH, each = 3),
                       c("DESeq2_species", "edgeR_species",
                         "metagenomeSeq_species"))

mypath_res <- RES_DIR
dir.create(OUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

## Name every missing input NOW rather than three calls deep inside a loader.
for (d in c(DATA_DIR, RES_DIR, MATRIX_DIR, TITAN_DIR, DA_DIRS))
  cat(sprintf("  %-8s %s\n", if (dir.exists(d)) "OK" else "MISSING",
              sub(PROJECT, "<project>", d, fixed = TRUE)))
if (!dir.exists(DATA_DIR))
  stop("Data folder not found. Download and unpack the Zenodo data deposit and set PAPER_DATA to it, or run:\n  bash stage_submission_data.sh\n",
       "It copies every input this document reads and writes the harmonised ",
       "metadata.", call. = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(dir.exists(c(DATA_DIR, RES_DIR, MATRIX_DIR, TITAN_DIR))))

## Stand-alone R scripts called with Rscript (Table 1 order check, within-soil effects and Fig. 4 tests, traits)
CODE_DIR <- getwd()
run_script <- function(script, ...) {
  st <- system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), c(file.path(CODE_DIR, script), shQuote(c(...))), stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(attr(st, "status")) && attr(st, "status") != 0) stop(paste(st, collapse = "\n"))
  invisible(st)
}
SUPP_DIR <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "supporting"); dir.create(SUPP_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r parameters}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Every threshold in the paper, in one place. These MUST match the Methods.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
PREV_MIN  <- 0.10        # taxon present in >= 10% of pots
ABUND_MIN <- 1e-4        # mean relative abundance >= 0.01%
MAX_TAXA  <- 200         # candidate-pool cap (search cost; Methods 2.6.2)
KFOLD     <- 5           # cross-validation folds
NPERM     <- 999         # PERMANOVA permutations
NPERM_NULL <- 50         # quick shuffled-biomass null inside table_s7(); the reported null (999 runs) is in 3.2.2
CP_MIN    <- 0.35        # TITAN2 change point (g) defining "high-biomass"
PURITY    <- 0.95        # inclusive (>=), as in Methods 2.6.2
RELIAB    <- 0.95
MIN_POTS  <- 3           # species with fewer pots excluded from species means
RESP      <- "Dry_wheat_mass"
DA_CONTROL <- "wheat x wheat"

SOILS    <- c(cereal = "resistant", mixed = "Permissive")  # metadata codes
SOILKEY  <- c(cereal = "soilA",     mixed = "soilB")       # export filenames
SOILNAME <- c(cereal = "Cereal-dominated (AF193)",
              mixed  = "Mixed-system (AF190)")

set.seed(20260917)   # fixed before any stochastic step
```

```{r load-data}
## The two community objects, built from the deposited tables. There are no
## serialised .rds objects in the project, so they are assembled here -- which
## is better for a reader anyway: the object's provenance is visible.
##
## The abundance tables are already rarefied (Methods: 7,000 bacterial and
## them to physeq_bacteria_raw / physeq_fungi_raw before 3.1.1: the normalisation
## sensitivity check needs them, and you cannot un-rarefy.
##
build_physeq <- function(otu_f, tax_f, meta_f) {
  otu  <- read.delim(file.path(MATRIX_DIR, otu_f),  row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
  tax  <- read.delim(file.path(MATRIX_DIR, tax_f),  row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
  meta <- read.csv(  file.path(MATRIX_DIR, meta_f), check.names = FALSE)
  stopifnot(ncol(otu) > 1)          # a 1-column matrix means the wrong delimiter
  rownames(meta) <- meta$sample
  keep <- intersect(colnames(otu), rownames(meta))
  phyloseq(otu_table(as.matrix(otu[, keep]), taxa_are_rows = TRUE),
           tax_table(as.matrix(tax[rownames(otu), , drop = FALSE])),
           sample_data(meta[keep, , drop = FALSE]))
}
physeq_bacteria <- build_physeq("otu_bacteria_table_R_1314ASVs.csv",
                                "tax_bacteria_R_1314ASVs.csv",
                                "metadata_bacteria_1314ASVs.csv")
physeq_fungi    <- build_physeq("otu_fungi_table_R_647ASVs.csv",
                                "tax_fungi_R_647ASVs.csv",
                                "metadata_fungi_647ASVs.csv")

## as.data.frame() on a phyloseq sample_data object returns something that
## still carries the S4 class, and adonis2() rejects it with
##   Error in terms.formula(formula, data = data): 'data' argument is of the
##   wrong type
## as(x, "data.frame") strips the class properly. data.frame() also works.
metadata_bacteria <- as(sample_data(physeq_bacteria), "data.frame")
metadata_fungi    <- as(sample_data(physeq_fungi),    "data.frame")
stopifnot(identical(class(metadata_bacteria), "data.frame"))

## Harmonise the three superseded binomials in the bacterial metadata onto the
## metadata (all 30 per-species replicate counts match exactly, against 5 of 30
## for the alternative soil pairing), and after this substitution the bacterial
## and fungal species sets are identical.
SYNONYMS <- c("Centaurea cyanus"    = "Cyanus segetum",
              "Festuca arundinacea" = "Lolium arundinaceum",
              "Bromus sterilis"     = "Anisantha sterilis",
              ## two wrong Poaceae labels in the DESeq2 / metagenomeSeq / old edgeR exports
              ## (row counts and raw-abundance correlation; da_consensus.py label check).
              ## Absent from the metadata, so harmless there.
              "Festuca myuros"      = "Lolium arundinaceum",
              "Viola arvensis"      = "Vulpia myuros")
for (m in c("metadata_bacteria", "metadata_fungi")) {
  d <- get(m); hit <- d$species %in% names(SYNONYMS)
  d$species[hit] <- SYNONYMS[d$species[hit]]
  d$species <- factor(d$species)
  assign(m, d)
}
sample_data(physeq_bacteria)$species <- metadata_bacteria$species
sample_data(physeq_fungi)$species    <- metadata_fungi$species
stopifnot(setequal(levels(metadata_bacteria$species),
                   levels(metadata_fungi$species)))

cat(sprintf("bacteria: %d taxa x %d samples\nfungi:    %d taxa x %d samples\n",
            ntaxa(physeq_bacteria), nsamples(physeq_bacteria),
            ntaxa(physeq_fungi), nsamples(physeq_fungi)))
```

# 3.1 Drivers of wheat root microbiota composition

## 3.1.1 Community composition and assembly

### Table 1, Fig. 1b: sequential PERMANOVA

```{r table-1}
bacteria_bray <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_bacteria, "bray")
fungi_bray    <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_fungi,    "bray")

set.seed(1)
bacteria_sequential <- adonis2(bacteria_bray ~ soil * species,
                               data = metadata_bacteria,
                               permutations = NPERM, by = "terms")
set.seed(1)
fungi_sequential    <- adonis2(fungi_bray ~ soil * species,
                               data = metadata_fungi,
                               permutations = NPERM, by = "terms")

tab1 <- permanova_table(list(`Bacteria (rpoB)` = bacteria_sequential,
                             `Fungi (ITS1)`    = fungi_sequential))
write.csv(tab1, file.path(OUT_DIR, "Table1_variance_partition.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
permanova_table_pretty(tab1, nperm = NPERM)
```

```{r fig-1b-partition}
## The partition percentages the Fig. 1 panel and the graphical abstract use.
## Written to CSV so the figure cannot drift from the table above.
## partition_from_adonis(bact_fit, fung_fit, labels) takes the two fits
## POSITIONALLY. Wrapping them in a list() passes one argument where two are
## expected, and the failure surfaces far from the cause as
##   arguments imply differing number of rows: 1, 4, 0
part <- partition_from_adonis(bacteria_sequential, fungi_sequential)
write.csv(part, file.path(OUT_DIR, "variance_partition.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
part
```

```{r normalisation}
## The compositional objection: does the partition survive a compositional
## distance (CLR / Aitchison) instead of Bray-Curtis on rarefied counts?
##
## compare_normalisations(ps, label, ...) takes ONE community object plus a
## character label -- not both objects. Passing the second object as `label`
## satisfies the arity, so there is no argument error; it fails much later with
##   rep(value, length.out = nrows): attempt to replicate an object of type 'S4'
## when the label is assigned into a data-frame column. Run it per kingdom.
cmp <- list(
  bacteria = compare_normalisations(physeq_bacteria, "Bacteria (rpoB)",
                                    permutations = NPERM),
  fungi    = compare_normalisations(physeq_fungi,    "Fungi (ITS1)",
                                    permutations = NPERM))

## report_normalisation() takes one result, so map over them.
invisible(lapply(cmp, report_normalisation))

## Write the long form of both -- $wide is the display table, $long carries
## every term x normalisation row the objection needs to be answerable.
norm_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cmp, `[[`, "long"))
write.csv(norm_long, file.path(OUT_DIR, "normalisation_sensitivity.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
data.frame(kingdom    = sapply(cmp, `[[`, "label"),
           max_shift_pp = sapply(cmp, `[[`, "max_shift"),
           zero_replacement = sapply(cmp, `[[`, "zero_replacement"),
           row.names  = NULL)
```

### Fig. S4: multivariate dispersion (PERMDISP)

```{r fig-s4-permdisp, fig.width = 7.2, fig.height = 6.4}
set.seed(20260917)   # permutest() draws permutations: fix them per chunk
## PERMDISP: is a PERMANOVA 'location' effect really a difference in spread?
## betadisper() places every sample in PCoA space (Bray-Curtis, negative
## eigenvalues handled by vegan), takes its distance to the SPATIAL MEDIAN of its
## group (type = "median", the vegan default and what the Results state), and
## an ANOVA on those distances is tested by permutation (permutest, 999).
## Both factors of Table 1 are tested, soil and neighbour species, in both
## kingdoms: Fig. S4 shows all four.
SOIL_COL <- c("Cereal-dominated (AF193)" = "#4C6E9E",   # same palette as Fig. 1 / Fig. S7
              "Mixed-system (AF190)"     = "#C4713A")
permdisp_one <- function(ps, kingdom, factor) {
  meta <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")
  D    <- vegan::vegdist(t(as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")), method = "bray")
  g    <- if (factor == "soil") factor(SOILNAME[match(meta$soil, SOILS)], levels = SOILNAME)
          else droplevels(factor(meta$species))
  bd   <- vegan::betadisper(D, g, type = "median")
  pt   <- vegan::permutest(bd, permutations = NPERM)
  tab  <- pt$tab
  list(test = data.frame(kingdom = kingdom, factor = factor,
                         df1 = tab$Df[1], df2 = tab$Df[2], F = tab$F[1],
                         p_perm = tab$`Pr(>F)`[1], n = length(g)),
       dist = data.frame(kingdom = kingdom, factor = factor, sample = rownames(meta),
                         group = as.character(g), soil = SOILNAME[match(meta$soil, SOILS)],
                         distance = as.numeric(bd$distances)))
}
pd_res <- list(); k <- 0
for (kg in c("bacteria", "fungi")) {
  ps <- if (kg == "bacteria") physeq_bacteria else physeq_fungi
  for (fc in c("soil", "species")) { k <- k + 1; pd_res[[k]] <- permdisp_one(ps, kg, fc) }
}
permdisp_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pd_res, `[[`, "test"))
permdisp_dist  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pd_res, `[[`, "dist"))
write.csv(permdisp_tests, file.path(OUT_DIR, "permdisp_tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(permdisp_dist,  file.path(OUT_DIR, "permdisp_distances.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
print(permdisp_tests, digits = 3)

lab_test <- function(kg, fc) {
  r <- permdisp_tests[permdisp_tests$kingdom == kg & permdisp_tests$factor == fc, ]
  sprintf("F[%d,%d] = %.2f, p = %.2f", r$df1, r$df2, r$F, r$p_perm)
}
KLAB <- c(bacteria = "Bacteria (rpoB)", fungi = "Fungi (ITS)")
pan_soil <- function(kg) {
  d <- permdisp_dist[permdisp_dist$kingdom == kg & permdisp_dist$factor == "soil", ]
  ggplot(d, aes(group, distance, fill = group)) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.55, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.55, colour = "grey25") +
    geom_jitter(aes(colour = group), width = 0.12, size = 0.7, alpha = 0.45) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = SOIL_COL, guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = SOIL_COL, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) sub(" \\(", "\n(", x)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Distance to spatial median\n(Bray-Curtis PCoA)",
         title = KLAB[[kg]], subtitle = paste("Soil:", lab_test(kg, "soil"))) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 8) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
}
pan_species <- function(kg) {
  d <- permdisp_dist[permdisp_dist$kingdom == kg & permdisp_dist$factor == "species", ]
  ord <- d %>% group_by(group) %>% summarise(m = median(distance)) %>% arrange(m) %>% pull(group)
  d$group <- factor(d$group, levels = ord)
  ggplot(d, aes(group, distance)) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "grey88", colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_jitter(aes(colour = soil), width = 0.15, size = 0.55, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = SOIL_COL, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Distance to spatial median",
         subtitle = paste("Neighbour species:", lab_test(kg, "species"))) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 8) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 55, hjust = 1, face = "italic", size = 6),
          legend.position = "top")
}
if (requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(patchwork)
  figS4 <- (pan_soil("bacteria") | pan_species("bacteria")) /
           (pan_soil("fungi")    | pan_species("fungi")) +
           plot_layout(widths = c(1, 4)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
  ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "FigS4_permdisp.png"), figS4, width = 7.2, height = 6.4, dpi = 400)
}
```

### Fig. S5: α-diversity

```{r fig-s5-alpha}
alpha_of <- function(ps, label) {
  d <- data.frame(sample = sample_names(ps),
                  richness = phyloseq::estimate_richness(ps, measures = "Observed")[,1],
                  shannon  = phyloseq::estimate_richness(ps, measures = "Shannon")[,1])
  md <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps)); d <- cbind(d, md[, c("soil", "species")])
  d$kingdom <- label
  d
}
alpha_b <- alpha_of(physeq_bacteria, "Bacteria (rpoB)")
alpha_f <- alpha_of(physeq_fungi,    "Fungi (ITS1)")
write.csv(rbind(alpha_b, alpha_f), file.path(OUT_DIR, "alpha_diversity.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

## omega-squared rather than eta-squared: less biased for a fixed-effects
## design, and it is what the text quotes.
omega2_table <- function(d, resp = "richness") {
  m <- aov(as.formula(paste(resp, "~ soil * species")), data = d)
  a <- summary(m)[[1]]
  msr <- a["Residuals", "Mean Sq"]; sst <- sum(a[, "Sum Sq"])
  data.frame(term = trimws(rownames(a)), df = a[, "Df"], F = a[, "F value"],
             p = a[, "Pr(>F)"],
             omega2 = (a[, "Sum Sq"] - a[, "Df"] * msr) / (sst + msr))
}
for (d in list(alpha_b, alpha_f)) {
  cat("\n--", d$kingdom[1], "-- observed richness\n")
  print(omega2_table(d, "richness"), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
}
```

### Fig. S7: βNTI and NST, bacteria (Methods S2)

```{r fig-s7-nst}
NST_DIR <- if (dir.exists(file.path(DATA_DIR, "NST"))) file.path(DATA_DIR, "NST") else
             file.path(PROJECT, "paper_1", "data", "NST")
nst <- list(
  tNST_bacteria = read.csv(file.path(NST_DIR, "NST_bacteria.csv")),
  tNST_fungi    = read.csv(file.path(NST_DIR, "NST_fungi.csv")),
  pNST_bacteria = read.csv(file.path(NST_DIR, "pNST_bacteria.csv")),
  pNST_fungi    = read.csv(file.path(NST_DIR, "pnst_fungi.csv")))
nst_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(nst), function(nm) {
  d <- nst[[nm]]; v <- if ("pNST" %in% names(d)) d$pNST else d$NST
  data.frame(index = sub("_.*", "", nm), kingdom = sub(".*_", "", nm), n_groups = sum(!is.na(v)),
             mean = mean(v, na.rm = TRUE), median = median(v, na.rm = TRUE),
             min = min(v, na.rm = TRUE), max = max(v, na.rm = TRUE),
             share_below_0.5 = mean(v < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
             weighting = if ("mode" %in% names(d)) paste(unique(d$mode), collapse = ",") else "bray, abundance-weighted")
}))
write.csv(nst_summary, file.path(OUT_DIR, "nst_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
print(nst_summary, digits = 3)
## The NST files also hold a 'Geranium pusillum' group, which is not in the design; it is dropped from Fig. S7.
## Fungal values are summarised here but not interpreted: ITS1 cannot be aligned across fungal phyla (Methods S2).
```

## 3.1.2 Neighbour-enriched taxa

Inputs for Fig. 2 and Table S3 (drawn in the notebook, which also runs the control-size check, `pooled_check.R`): edgeR contrasts against wheat × wheat, and the fold-change orientation of every export.

```{r edger-vs-wheat-x-wheat}
## built from the same 1,314- / 647-ASV tables that da_consensus.py and Table 2 read
ps_da <- function(kg) {
  tag  <- if (kg == "bacteria") "1314" else "647"
  otu  <- read.delim(file.path(MATRIX_DIR, sprintf("otu_%s_table_R_%sASVs.csv", kg, tag)), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
  meta <- read.csv(file.path(MATRIX_DIR, sprintf("metadata_%s_%sASVs.csv", kg, tag)), check.names = FALSE)
  rownames(meta) <- meta$sample; keep <- intersect(colnames(otu), rownames(meta))
  phyloseq(otu_table(as.matrix(otu[, keep]), taxa_are_rows = TRUE), sample_data(meta[keep, ]))
}
DA_EXPORT_DIR <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "da_exports", "edgeR_species")
dir.create(DA_EXPORT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
edger_n <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("bacteria", "fungi"), function(kg) {
  ps <- ps_da(kg)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c(Resistant = SOILS[["cereal"]], Permissive = SOILS[["mixed"]]), function(code) {
    tag <- if (code == SOILS[["cereal"]]) "Resistant" else "Permissive"
    r <- edger_vs_control(ps, code)
    write.csv(r, file.path(DA_EXPORT_DIR, sprintf("edgeR_%s_%s_vs_wheat_x_wheat.csv", kg, tag)), row.names = TRUE)
    data.frame(kingdom = kg, soil = tag, taxa_tested = attr(r, "n_taxa_tested"),
               rows_exported = nrow(r), neighbours = length(unique(r$comparison)))
  }))
}))
edger_n
```

```{r da-orientation}
set.seed(20260917)
orient_one <- function(ps, f, method, soil_code) {
  d <- read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE)
  X <- t(as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")); X <- X / rowSums(X) * 7000
  meta <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")
  ctrl <- rownames(meta)[meta$soil == soil_code & meta$species == "wheat x wheat"]
  raw <- function(w) {
    a <- rownames(meta)[meta$soil == soil_code & meta$species == w]
    if (!length(a)) return(NULL)
    log2((colMeans(X[a, , drop = FALSE]) + 0.5) / (colMeans(X[ctrl, , drop = FALSE]) + 0.5))
  }
  if (method == "metagenomeSeq") {
    k <- as.character(d[[1]])
    d$weed <- gsub(".", " ", sub("\\.Cluster_[0-9]+$", "", k), fixed = TRUE)
    d$taxa <- sub("^.*\\.(Cluster_[0-9]+)$", "\\1", k); d$lfc <- d[["NA"]]
  } else {
    d <- split_comparison(d)
    d <- d[d$species1 == "wheat x wheat" | d$species2 == "wheat x wheat", ]
    if (!nrow(d)) return(data.frame(file = basename(f), n_neighbours = 0, median_r = NA,
                                    ids_in_table = NA, verdict = "control absent"))
    d$weed <- ifelse(d$species1 == "wheat x wheat", d$species2, d$species1)
    d$lfc  <- if (method == "DESeq2") d$log2FoldChange else d$logFC
  }
  d$weed[d$weed %in% names(SYNONYMS)] <- SYNONYMS[d$weed[d$weed %in% names(SYNONYMS)]]
  r <- sapply(split(d, d$weed), function(g) {
    rr <- raw(g$weed[1]); if (is.null(rr)) return(NA)
    ok <- g$taxa %in% names(rr); if (sum(ok) < 10) return(NA)
    suppressWarnings(cor(g$lfc[ok], rr[g$taxa[ok]]))
  })
  m <- median(r, na.rm = TRUE)
  data.frame(file = basename(f), n_neighbours = sum(!is.na(r)), median_r = round(m, 2),
             ids_in_table = round(mean(unique(d$taxa) %in% taxa_names(ps)), 2),
             verdict = if (is.na(m) || abs(m) < 0.5) "REFUSE: other numbering or mislabelled"
                       else if (m > 0) "log2(neighbour / control)" else "log2(control / neighbour)")
}
orient <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("Resistant", "Permissive"), function(tag) {
  code <- if (tag == "Resistant") SOILS[["cereal"]] else SOILS[["mixed"]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c(RES_DIR, DATA_DIR), function(root) {
    fs <- c(DESeq2 = file.path(root, "DESeq2_species", sprintf("DESeq_bacteria_%s_species_vs_wheat_x_wheat_pval.csv", tag)),
            edgeR  = file.path(root, "edgeR_species",  sprintf("edgeR_bacteria_%s_vs_wheat_x_wheat.csv", tag)),
            metagenomeSeq = file.path(root, "metagenomeSeq_species", sprintf("MetaSeq_bacteria_%s_CSS_wheat_x_wheat.csv", tag)))
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fs), function(m) if (file.exists(fs[[m]]))
      cbind(soil = tag, root = basename(root), method = m, orient_one(physeq_bacteria, fs[[m]], m, code))))
  }))
}))
write.csv(orient, file.path(OUT_DIR, "check_da_orientation.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
orient
```

# 3.2 Wheat performance and the microbiota

## 3.2.1 Wheat biomass

### Table S5: wheat biomass with total neighbour biomass (Fig. 3, Table S4 and the log-scale model: notebook 3.2.1)

```{r table-s5-biomass}
bio <- metadata_bacteria[!is.na(metadata_bacteria[[RESP]]), ]
m_bio <- aov(as.formula(paste(RESP, "~ soil * species")), data = bio)
print(summary(m_bio))

## Table S5: does total neighbour biomass (Btot) explain wheat biomass beyond
## neighbour identity? WEEDS ONLY: 'wheat alone' has no neighbour and 'wheat x
## wheat' is an intraspecific neighbour, so neither belongs on a weed-biomass axis
## Type II sums of squares, so the Btot
## test is adjusted for soil, species and their interaction, and each main
## effect for the other and for Btot. partial eta^2 = SS_Btot / (SS_Btot + SS_res).
stopifnot(requireNamespace("car", quietly = TRUE))   # Type II sums of squares
bio_w <- metadata_bacteria[!is.na(metadata_bacteria[[RESP]]) &
                         !is.na(metadata_bacteria$Adventice_dry_mass) &
                         !metadata_bacteria$species %in% c("wheat alone", "wheat x wheat"), ]
bio_w$species <- droplevels(factor(bio_w$species))
m_base <- lm(as.formula(paste0("log(", RESP, ") ~ soil * species")), data = bio_w)   # log scale, as the main model
m_cov  <- lm(as.formula(paste0("log(", RESP, ") ~ soil * species + Adventice_dry_mass")), data = bio_w)
s6 <- as.data.frame(car::Anova(m_cov, type = 2))
s6$partial_eta2 <- s6$`Sum Sq` / (s6$`Sum Sq` + s6["Residuals", "Sum Sq"])
s6["Residuals", "partial_eta2"] <- NA
attr(s6, "R2") <- c(base = summary(m_base)$r.squared, with_Btot = summary(m_cov)$r.squared)
write.csv(cbind(term = rownames(s6), s6), file.path(OUT_DIR, "Table_S6_biomass_ancova.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
print(s6, digits = 4)
cat(sprintf("n pots = %d, neighbour species = %d, R2 %.3f -> %.3f, Btot slope %.4f (SE %.4f)\n",
            nrow(bio_w), nlevels(bio_w$species), summary(m_base)$r.squared, summary(m_cov)$r.squared,
            coef(m_cov)[["Adventice_dry_mass"]], sqrt(diag(vcov(m_cov)))[["Adventice_dry_mass"]]))
write.csv(data.frame(model = c("soil * species", "soil * species + Btot"),
                     R2 = c(summary(m_base)$r.squared, summary(m_cov)$r.squared),
                     n = nrow(bio_w)), file.path(OUT_DIR, "Table_S6_model_R2.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

### TITAN2 (Methods 2.8, Methods S3)

```{r titan2}
## purity and reliability >= 0.95, change point >= CP_MIN. Both directions:
## maxgrp == 2 is z+ (increases above the change point), maxgrp == 1 is z-.
titan <- lapply(names(SOILKEY), function(s)
  lapply(c("bacteria", "fungi"), function(kg)
    titan_flagged(file.path(TITAN_DIR,
                            sprintf("%s_titan_%s_results_v3.csv", kg, SOILKEY[[s]])),
                  cp_min = CP_MIN, purity_min = PURITY,
                  reliability_min = RELIAB)))
names(titan) <- names(SOILKEY)
str(titan, max.level = 2)
```

```{r titan2-change-points}
cp_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("bacteria", "fungi"), function(kg)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(SOILKEY), function(s) {
    d <- read.csv(file.path(TITAN_DIR, sprintf("%s_titan_%s_results_v3.csv", kg, SOILKEY[[s]])),
                  check.names = FALSE)
    q  <- d[d$purity >= PURITY & d$reliability >= RELIAB, ]
    hb <- q[q$`ienv.cp` >= CP_MIN, ]
    data.frame(kingdom = kg, soil = SOILNAME[[s]], tested = nrow(d), pure_reliable = nrow(q),
               retained = nrow(hb), z_plus = sum(hb$maxgrp == 2), z_minus = sum(hb$maxgrp == 1),
               cp_min = round(min(hb$`ienv.cp`), 3), cp_max = round(max(hb$`ienv.cp`), 3))
  }))))
y <- metadata_bacteria[[RESP]]
cat(sprintf("observed wheat biomass: %.3f-%.3f g (5th-95th percentile %.3f-%.3f g)\n",
            min(y, na.rm = TRUE), max(y, na.rm = TRUE),
            quantile(y, .05, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(y, .95, na.rm = TRUE)))
write.csv(cp_rows, file.path(OUT_DIR, "check_titan_changepoints.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cp_rows
```

### Table S7: TITAN2 indicators of wheat biomass (exploratory, pot level)

```{r table-s6-titan2}
## The filter thresholds are NOT arguments here -- table_s5() reads PREV_MIN,
## ABUND_MIN, MAX_TAXA and CP_MIN from the global environment, which the
## `parameters` chunk above sets. Passing them errors with "unused arguments".
s5 <- table_s5(physeq_bacteria, physeq_fungi, titan_dir = TITAN_DIR,
               meqo_dir = MEQO_DIR, soils = SOILS)
## table_s5() fills Genus only for mEQO selections (it takes it from the mEQO export),
## which left 114 of 154 rows blank -- including the two taxa Discussion 4.2 names
## (Cluster_431 Sphingomonas, Cluster_358 Massilia). Fill every row from the
## taxonomy tables of the 1,314- / 647-ASV set.
s5_genus <- function(kg) {
  f <- file.path(MATRIX_DIR, sprintf("tax_%s_R_%sASVs.csv", kg, if (kg == "bacteria") "1314" else "647"))
  tx <- read.delim(f, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
  setNames(as.character(tx$Genus), rownames(tx))
}
for (kg in c("bacteria", "fungi")) {
  i <- s5$kingdom == kg; g <- s5_genus(kg)[as.character(s5$ASV[i])]
  s5$Genus[i] <- ifelse(is.na(s5$Genus[i]) | s5$Genus[i] == "", g, s5$Genus[i])
}
stopifnot(!any(is.na(s5$Genus) | s5$Genus == ""))
write.csv(s5, file.path(OUT_DIR, "Table_S5_biomass_associated_taxa.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("Table S7 source: %d rows (TITAN2 taxa; legacy mEQO columns, if present, are dropped in the notebook)\n", nrow(s5)))
head(s5, 10)
```
